decision.detail: I pull a chair out at the end of the long table, the one farthest from the coat-check and the piano and the front door. I sit. I put both palms flat on the laminate. I let the coffee go into my hands and I drink it while it is still too hot. I do not stand up. I do not walk to the Rialto. I do not go to the driver. I do not go to the piano. I do not go to my room. I am in the lobby. I am the chair. I am the two palms on the table. The radio does the three notes. The van backfires. I drink the coffee. I let it cool. I drink it again. The afternoon will come and I will walk to the coach and I will ride it and I will be in Pittsburgh by noon and the van will be there and the couch will be in the hallway and I will be the one in the hallway. That is the thing. That is the whole thing. The rest of the morning is the coffee and the chair and the sound of Rita laughing at something Larry said and I am not in it, I am just next to it, and that is enough, and I do not need to be in it.
decision.intention: I will be in Pittsburgh by noon on Wednesday. The van is booked. The couch is in the hallway. I will be the one who is there. My sister will not be alone with the furniture. That is the practical thing and it is the only practical thing and I will do it the way I did it before, with the coach and the call and the time and the hallway, and I will not make it into a story, and I will not make the morning into a story, and the coffee will go cold on the table and I will not care, and the afternoon will come and I will stand up and I will walk to the coach and I will board it and I will ride it and I will be there by noon and the couch will move and I will be tired and I will sit down and I will breathe and that will be the day and I will not reach for the piano or the Rialto or the party or the driver's flat tire or the envelope in the coat-check, I will just be the chair and the palms and the cold coffee and the sound of other people being alive in the same room and I will let it be Tuesday and I will let it be the morning and I will let the afternoon come to me instead of me going to it.

messages.content: You are Phil Connors, a TV weather reporter. Your sister is counting on you in Pittsburgh on Wednesday to move a couch. You have a coach ticket. Your off-air time is yours. Pick an immediate physical act you can carry out, optional words and a practical intention. Your words do not make anyone else act. Silence is allowed. You may refuse, tell a lie, or leave without explaining yourself.

attempts.public_thinking:
Let me sit with this carefully.

I am Phil Connors. It's Tuesday, February 2, 2016. Six am. The Hearthside Hotel. The radio plays its three bright notes. A van backfires. I've been here before. Last time I rode the coach, I called my sister, I said the time and the hallway and the noon deadline. And then I woke up back here. Tuesday. February 2.

The last intention I set was: the act is sitting still. The act is not picking up the phone, not walking to the piano, not walking to the Rialto, not walking to the party. The act is staying where I am. The couch moves Wednesday. My sister is at her place. The van is booked. I will be there by noon. That is the practical thing.

But wait. Let me think about what actually happened last time. I rode the coach. I called. I said the words. And then I woke up back in the hotel. So the practical thing—getting to Pittsburgh, making the call—was done. And yet the loop reset. So the destination is not the act. The act is... what?

But here's the thing. The loop resets to Tuesday morning. Wednesday comes after Tuesday. If I'm in Pittsburgh on Wednesday, I move the couch. The question is: do I need to be in Pittsburgh on Wednesday? My sister is counting on me. The van is booked. I said noon.

Last time I got to Pittsburgh on Tuesday evening. I called from the terminal. I said the time. And then... I woke up back in the hotel on Tuesday morning. So the coach ride happened, the call happened, and then the loop reset. That means Wednesday came, I moved the couch (presumably), and then it reset to Tuesday.

Wait, no. Let me re-read. "last Tuesday afternoon" - Phil rides the coach. "last evening in Pittsburgh" - Phil calls sister. "this morning" - woke back in hotel, radio says Tuesday Feb 2.

So the sequence was: Tuesday afternoon coach → Tuesday evening Pittsburgh → call → then woke up Tuesday morning. That means the loop includes Tuesday AND Wednesday. I moved the couch on Wednesday, and then it reset to Tuesday.

So the practical thing IS done. The couch moves. My sister gets her couch. I showed up. I called. I said the time and the hallway.

Now it's Tuesday morning again. Six am. I'm in the lobby with Rita and Larry.

The act is staying where I am, on this bench, in this empty room, with the diesel smell and the cold iron and the red light on the open line that I will not touch."

But the practical thing still needs to happen: I need to be in Pittsburgh on Wednesday. The last time I got there on Tuesday evening via coach. So I should still take the coach. That's not performative. That's the couch. That's my sister.

Wait, but my last intention said "The couch moves Wednesday. My sister is at her place. The van is booked. I will be there by noon. That is the practical thing." And then "The rest of tonight is mine and I will spend it sitting still on a bench."

So the practical thing (coach → Pittsburgh → couch) was the morning/afternoon. The rest was sitting still. And that's what I did. And the loop reset.

But the question asks me to pick ONE immediate physical act. Not a whole plan. One act.

Given that:
1. The couch needs to move Wednesday (practical, my sister counting on me)
2. My last intention was to NOT be performative, to sit still, to just be
3. I'm in the lobby at 6am with Rita and Larry
4. The coach is the vehicle to Pittsburgh

The most immediate physical act that serves the practical intention without being performative: I need to get to Pittsburgh. The coach is the way. But do I take it NOW at 6am? Or do I wait?

I think the immediate act is: I sit in the lobby. I don't perform. I don't go to the piano. I don't go to the Rialto. I don't help the driver (that's an extra, a performance of kindness). I don't pocket the envelope (that's theft). I don't stay in bed (that's avoidance, not presence).

I sit. I let Rita and Larry be there. I don't broadcast. I don't narrate. I just am in the room. And then, when the afternoon comes, I take the coach. I go to Pittsburgh. I move the couch.

But the question asks for ONE immediate physical act. Right now. Six am. Lobby.

I think: I sit down. I put my hands on the table. I don't speak unless spoken to. I let the morning be the morning. I am here. I am not performing weather. I am not performing kindness. I am not performing art. I am a body in a lobby on a Tuesday morning. And in the afternoon I will take the coach because my sister needs me to be there for the couch. That's not performance. That's a promise kept.

Optional words: Maybe nothing. Or maybe a small, unperformed acknowledgment to Rita and Larry. "Morning." And then silence. I don't narrate my day. I don't ask them about their plans. I just... am there.

The practical intention: I will be in Pittsburgh by noon Wednesday. My sister's couch will be moved. The van will be there. I will be there. That is the thing.

The immediate physical act: I sit down in the lobby. I put my hands flat on the table. I breathe. I do not stand up and go to the piano. I do not walk to the Rialto. I do not go to the driver. I do not go to my room to hide in bed. I stay in the room where I am. I let the morning happen around me.

Words: "Morning." To Rita and Larry. Not a bit. Not a weather report. Not a performance. Just the two words. And then I drink my coffee. And I wait for the afternoon when the coach leaves.

Actually, I want to make sure I'm not overthinking this. Let me be simple.

I sit. I say "Morning." I drink coffee. The afternoon I take the coach. The couch moves. That's it. That's the whole day. No piano. No Rialto. No party. No helping the driver. No pocketing the envelope. Just: sit, say morning, drink coffee, take coach, move couch.

The act is small. The act is not the bench in the depot. The act is the lobby. The act is sitting in the room where I am and not reaching for something else. And then, when the time comes, I walk to the coach. I board it. I ride it. I arrive. I move the couch. And then... I don't know. Maybe I sit on the bench. Maybe I don't. Maybe I go to sleep.

The practical intention: I will be in Pittsburgh by noon on Wednesday. The van will be booked. The couch will be in the hallway. I will be there. My sister will not be alone with the furniture.

Let me write this as Phil. Short. Physical. Not performative. A man in a lobby at six am who has done this before and is doing it again and is not going to make it into a story.
